I think it needs a bit of a rewrite, probably by a native English speaker, for it to make a bit more sense.

While I understood what was happening after reading it, it took reading the comments to really "get" it.

Like, for example:

The sculpture is approximately (last tape measure in Area 22/13 was lost during Incident ██.██.20██) 1.5 meters tall and can be carried by four (4) properly fed Foundation employees.

That could be clarified a bit better. Maybe something like:

The sculpture is approximately 1.5 meters in height (approximation due to last tape measure in Area 22/13 being lost during Incident ██.██.20██). Weight is unknown, but it can be carried by four (4) fit and well-fed Foundation employees (should any be present in Area 22/13).

The 80-proof amnestic and the fact that the only visual representation of it is an accountant's drawing, however, are both comic gold.

item.content:encoded:
A quote from a wonderful, incredibly intelligent man:

…when you make a joke and no one laughs; you then explain the joke and everyone goes "Oh, that's pretty clever, I guess," but they still won't laugh because you didn't tell the joke right in the first place!

Even if I put myself in the position of getting the joke when I first read it, while I understand how it can be seen as funny, I feel like the joke doesn't fit on this site. The focus of this article (and the joke) was the lack of budget and such, not the actual object that was supposed to be the SCP - the SCP object could have been replaced with virtually anything (that isn't anomalous) and the joke would have been exactly the same had the same effect. Even in the SCP-J's, the articles (and jokes) are supposed to be about the object being contained, not the circumstances surrounding it.

Don't get me wrong, it's a good satire; it just doesn't belong here, IMHO. Downvoted for being inappropriate for the site.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
…hahahahaha :D

So the report is a thinly disguised "fuck you" from the Russian site1 lambasting the higher-ups for basically abandoning them/forgetting about them due to bureaucratic rather than anomalous means. I also like the implication that the statue isn't actually anomalous, but rather those two researchers just started having reasonable-under-the-circumstances nightmares about their boss, and attributed them to the statue instead of hunger/fatigue/PTSD/whatever.

As a note for people who don't get the background: after the collapse of the USSR, there were many, many military outposts that went without pay or resupply for extensive lengths of time. My understanding (and please correct me if I'm wrong, Gene R) is that there were a lot of defections during that period, and a lot of soldiers only stayed because at least they were getting someplace to sleep.

Footnotes
1. The in-universe Site, not the wiki site.
